title: SLI validation query scratchpad (logs vs metrics) — tiered SLOs
content:
Context
- Purpose: validate SLI computations by comparing canonical metrics (Prometheus) to raw-ish logs (BQ export) across tier/region/model/route.
- This is a scratchpad; queries are for spot checks + gap analysis (NOT yet production dashboards).
- Primary use: confirm Hosted vs Dedicated SLI math before we lock SLO targets + burn-rate alerts.

Assumptions / glossary
- “Metrics” = redwood_* Prometheus time series emitted by gateway/routing/runtime.
- “Logs” = gateway structured request logs + routing decision logs exported to BigQuery.
- Tier dimension: tier={hosted|dedicated} expected to be consistent end-to-end after tier propagation changes (ref: redwood PR #18433). Until that lands everywhere, tier may be missing or inferred.
- Timeouts:
  - Gateway timeout: gateway gives up waiting for upstream (often 504).
  - Upstream/runtime timeout: runtime returns deadline exceeded mapped to 5xx/timeout class.
  - Customer-side timeout: client gives up (often shows as 499 / client_abort). Exclude from availability SLI.
- Streaming endpoints: need both TTFT and “stream completion” SLIs.

Known data quality issues (keep in mind during validation)
1) Miscounting 499/timeout in Hosted availability SLI
   - We saw 499 being counted as “server failure” in early Hosted SLI math; hotfix in PR #18544.
   - Validation action: re-run 2026-02-01..2026-02-10 window before/after hotfix; confirm 499 excluded from availability.

2) Streaming disconnect attribution is inconsistent across services
   - Before gateway classification changes (PR #18440), disconnects were lumped together.
   - Even after: some routes report disconnect reason in logs but metrics only have disconnect_total without reason.
   - Validation action: cross-tab disconnect_reason from logs vs disconnect_class label in metrics (if present).

3) Cardinality blowups / missing labels
   - Route/model labels are not always present or are high-cardinality (full model version strings, long routes).
   - Some services emit model as “requested_model” vs “resolved_model” (post-routing).
   - Validation action: prefer resolved_model for end-to-end SLIs; if missing, use route-level validation only.

4) Sampling
   - Some gateway logs are sampled under high QPS (dynamic sampling). Metrics are not.
   - Validation action: only compare ratios (error rate, disconnect rate) where sampling is uniform-ish; be careful comparing absolute counts.


What we’re validating (SLIs)
A) Availability / success rate (non-streaming)
- Numerator: successful responses (2xx/3xx) + “expected” 4xx? (depends on SLI definition; current plan is to exclude invalid requests from denominator rather than count as failures).
- Denominator: valid requests (excludes invalid auth, malformed payload, rate-limit rejects depending on policy).
- Failures: 5xx + server timeouts. Exclude client_abort (499) and customer timeouts (if detectable).

B) Availability / success rate (streaming)
- Two distinct SLIs:
  1) TTFT success + TTFT latency (time_to_first_token)
  2) Stream completion (no server-side disconnect) + disconnect rate

C) Latency
- Non-streaming: request_duration_ms p95/p99.
- Streaming: TTFT p95/p99 is the primary latency SLI; stream duration is mostly diagnostic (high variance by output length).

D) Dedicated pool readiness (FYI)
- Out of scope for this doc’s queries except sanity checks; the readiness signal will be validated separately with scheduler logs.


Data sources
Prometheus metrics (names approximate; confirm actual after instrumentation rollout)
- redwood_gateway_requests_total{tier,region,route,method,status_class}
- redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tier,region,route}
- redwood_gateway_stream_disconnects_total{tier,region,route,disconnect_class}
- redwood_runtime_ttft_seconds_bucket{tier,region,model}
- redwood_runtime_stream_disconnects_total{tier,region,model,disconnect_class}
- redwood_routing_fallback_total{tier,region,from_model,to_model,reason}

BigQuery tables (current working names; check with Logan)
- logs.gateway_requests_* (partitioned by date)
- logs.gateway_stream_events_* (start/ttft/end/disconnect)
- logs.routing_decisions_* (resolved_model, fallback info)


Validation workflow (recommended)
1) Pick a narrow scope first
   - 1 tier (hosted)
   - 1 region (us-east-1)
   - 1 route family (/v1/chat.completions streaming + /v1/embeddings)
   - 60-minute window (or 6h) to keep queries cheap.

2) Compare ratios, not raw counts
   - Because logs can be sampled and metrics are not.

3) Reconcile classification logic
   - Metrics use status_class labels (2xx/4xx/5xx) + explicit timeout/disconnect counters.
   - Logs may have HTTP status, upstream_status, grpc_status, error_reason.

4) Escalate mismatches
   - If mismatch is >0.2% absolute on success rate or >0.5% absolute on disconnect rate, open a thread + attach query outputs.


PromQL snippets (metrics)

(1) Hosted availability (non-streaming) — error rate by tier/region/route
- Goal: compute 1 - (5xx + timeout) / valid_requests

# Total requests excluding obviously-invalid categories (placeholder filters; adjust once labels exist)
sum by (tier, region, route) (
  rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{tier="hosted", status_class=~"2xx|3xx|4xx|5xx"}[5m])
)

# Server failures (5xx)
sum by (tier, region, route) (
  rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{tier="hosted", status_class="5xx"}[5m])
)

# Timeouts (if a separate metric exists)
sum by (tier, region, route) (
  rate(redwood_gateway_timeouts_total{tier="hosted"}[5m])
)

# Availability (simple form)
1 - (
  (sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{tier="hosted", status_class="5xx"}[5m]))
   + sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_gateway_timeouts_total{tier="hosted"}[5m])))
  /
  sum by (region, route) (rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{tier="hosted"}[5m]))
)

Notes:
- Need to confirm whether 429 (rate limiting) is excluded from denominator or treated as failure. Current SLO proposal leans: exclude from “availability” but track separately.
- Make sure 499 is NOT represented as 5xx. If status_class is derived incorrectly, fix at gateway.


(2) Streaming disconnect rate (Hosted) — by disconnect class
sum by (region, route, disconnect_class) (
  rate(redwood_gateway_stream_disconnects_total{tier="hosted"}[5m])
)
/
sum by (region, route) (
  rate(redwood_gateway_stream_starts_total{tier="hosted"}[5m])
)

Quick expectation:
- disconnect_class="client_abort" should be the majority during normal ops.
- disconnect_class="server_error" or "upstream_reset" spikes correlate with incidents; those are what we care about for SLI.


(3) TTFT p95 for streaming routes
histogram_quantile(0.95,
  sum by (le, region, route) (
    rate(redwood_runtime_ttft_seconds_bucket{tier="hosted"}[5m])
  )
)


BigQuery snippets (logs)

(1) Availability from gateway request logs (ratio)
- Compare to PromQL availability.

DECLARE start_ts TIMESTAMP DEFAULT TIMESTAMP("2026-02-20 18:00:00+00");
DECLARE end_ts   TIMESTAMP DEFAULT TIMESTAMP("2026-02-20 19:00:00+00");

WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    timestamp,
    region,
    -- tier may be missing; attempt to use logged tier first, else infer from auth/tenant type
    COALESCE(tier, IF(dedicated_pool_id IS NULL, "hosted", "dedicated")) AS tier_norm,
    route,
    http_status,
    error_reason,
    client_terminated,
    request_id
  FROM `redwood-prod.logs.gateway_requests_*`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN start_ts AND end_ts
    AND region = "us-east-1"
    AND route IN ("/v1/embeddings", "/v1/completions", "/v1/chat/completions")
)
SELECT
  tier_norm AS tier,
  region,
  route,
  COUNT(1) AS reqs,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN http_status BETWEEN 500 AND 599 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(1)) AS rate_5xx,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN http_status = 504 OR error_reason = "gateway_timeout" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(1)) AS rate_timeout,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN http_status = 499 OR client_terminated = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(1)) AS rate_client_abort
FROM base
WHERE tier_norm = "hosted"
  -- Proposed exclusions (adjust as SLI spec finalizes)
  AND NOT (http_status IN (401, 403) OR error_reason IN ("invalid_auth", "bad_api_key"))
  AND NOT (http_status IN (400, 404, 405) OR error_reason IN ("invalid_request", "schema_validation_failed"))
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY reqs DESC;

Interpretation:
- Compare rate_5xx + rate_timeout to the PromQL computed error ratio.
- rate_client_abort should NOT be included in SLI failure bucket.


(2) Streaming disconnect taxonomy from logs
- Goal: validate disconnect classification logic before metrics become canonical.

DECLARE start_ts TIMESTAMP DEFAULT TIMESTAMP("2026-02-20 18:00:00+00");
DECLARE end_ts   TIMESTAMP DEFAULT TIMESTAMP("2026-02-20 19:00:00+00");

WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    timestamp,
    region,
    COALESCE(tier, IF(dedicated_pool_id IS NULL, "hosted", "dedicated")) AS tier_norm,
    route,
    request_id,
    event_type, -- start | ttft | end | disconnect
    disconnect_reason,
    disconnect_at_ms,
    http_status,
    upstream_status
  FROM `redwood-prod.logs.gateway_stream_events_*`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN start_ts AND end_ts
    AND region = "us-east-1"
    AND route = "/v1/chat/completions"
)
SELECT
  tier_norm AS tier,
  region,
  route,
  disconnect_reason,
  COUNT(1) AS disconnects
FROM events
WHERE event_type = "disconnect"
  AND tier_norm = "hosted"
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
ORDER BY disconnects DESC;

Notes / gotchas:
- disconnect_reason can be empty for some disconnects; that’s a logging gap.
- If request_id can join to gateway_requests, add join to extract user-agent/client type (we’ve seen a few SDK-specific abort patterns).


(3) TTFT from logs (if available)
- Use stream events to compute TTFT distribution; compare to runtime TTFT metric.

DECLARE start_ts TIMESTAMP DEFAULT TIMESTAMP("2026-02-20 18:00:00+00");
DECLARE end_ts   TIMESTAMP DEFAULT TIMESTAMP("2026-02-20 19:00:00+00");

WITH starts AS (
  SELECT request_id, region, route, COALESCE(tier, IF(dedicated_pool_id IS NULL, "hosted", "dedicated")) AS tier_norm,
         MIN(timestamp) AS start_time
  FROM `redwood-prod.logs.gateway_stream_events_*`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN start_ts AND end_ts
    AND event_type = "start"
    AND route = "/v1/chat/completions"
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
),
first_token AS (
  SELECT request_id, MIN(timestamp) AS ttft_time
  FROM `redwood-prod.logs.gateway_stream_events_*`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN start_ts AND end_ts
    AND event_type = "ttft"
    AND route = "/v1/chat/completions"
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  s.tier_norm AS tier,
  s.region,
  s.route,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(f.ttft_time, s.start_time, MILLISECOND), 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS ttft_p95_ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(f.ttft_time, s.start_time, MILLISECOND), 100)[OFFSET(99)] AS ttft_p99_ms,
  COUNT(1) AS n
FROM starts s
JOIN first_token f USING (request_id)
WHERE s.tier_norm = "hosted"
GROUP BY 1,2,3;

Notes:
- If ttft event is emitted by gateway but runtime TTFT differs, expect a constant-ish offset (gateway overhead). Large variance suggests clock skew or mis-modeled event.


Sampling + cardinality notes (actionable)
- If we want per-model validation via logs, we should join to routing_decisions to get resolved_model.
  - But that join is expensive; do it only on a short window.
- Proposal for validation queries:
  - Prefer dimension set: {tier, region, route} for routine checks.
  - Only add {model} when investigating a specific incident/regression.
- For metrics:
  - Avoid emitting full model version strings (e.g., llama-3.1-70b-instruct-2026-02-xx). Use model_family + model_variant where possible.
  - Ensure route labels are normalized (no tenant IDs, no full URLs).


Mismatch checklist (when logs disagree with metrics)
1) Are logs sampled in the window? (check sampling flag if present; else look at sudden drops in total rows)
2) Is tier label missing? (infer tier and re-run; check rollout status of tier propagation)
3) Is 499 being counted as 5xx in metrics? (compare breakdown by status_class)
4) Are timeouts double-counted? (504 + timeout counter)
5) Are disconnects being emitted from both gateway and runtime? (possible double-count if SLI sums both)
6) Is the request counted twice due to retries? (logs may have both original + retried requests)


Open questions / TODO
- Decide final denominator rules:
  - Include/exclude 429 for availability? (lean exclude for availability SLI, include for “throttling rate” SLI)
  - Include/exclude 408? (rare; likely treat as client-side unless we can attribute to gateway)
- Establish canonical mapping table from (http_status, grpc_status, error_reason, disconnect_reason) -> error_class.
  - Add as a shared artifact so gateway + routing + runtime stay in sync.
- Add a small “validation harness” script that runs:
  - PromQL queries via API
  - BQ queries
  - outputs a diff report (ratios only) for a given scope.


Who to ping when you see an issue
- Label/tier propagation: Caleb Johnson / Amara Diallo
- Logs export & schema: Logan Wright
- Metric naming/cardinality: Thomas Baird
- SLI math + exclusions: Aisha Bello / Nadia Rahman
- Dashboards/alerting showing mismatch: Sergio Costa
